title: Gyeongju vs Andong: Which Should You Visit?
verdict: Gyeongju for first-timers and ease of access. Andong for deep cultural immersion, jimdak, and Hahoe Folk Village. Do both if you have 4+ days.

categories.name: Historical Sites
categories.summary: Gyeongju has 10+ major sites from the Silla Kingdom. Andong's Hahoe Folk Village is a living UNESCO heritage site.

categories.name: Food
categories.summary: Andong jimdak and traditional soju are destination-worthy. Gyeongju has hwangnam-ppang and beopju.

categories.name: Transit Access
categories.summary: Gyeongju has KTX connections from Busan and Seoul. Andong is bus-only with no KTX.

categories.name: Getting Around
categories.summary: Gyeongju is excellent by bicycle. Andong requires bus schedules for Hahoe Village.

categories.name: Budget
categories.summary: Andong is marginally cheaper: ~$37-60/day vs Gyeongju's ~$45-75/day.

categories.name: Crowds
categories.summary: Andong is genuinely off the beaten path. Gyeongju gets moderate tourist crowds.

categories.name: Best Season
categories.summary: Both peak in autumn (Oct-Nov). Andong's Mask Dance Festival is in October.

faq.question: Is Gyeongju or Andong better for first-time visitors?
faq.answer: Gyeongju — more sights, easier transit, highly recommended for Korean history lovers.

faq.question: How long do you need in Gyeongju?
faq.answer: 2 full days minimum to see city sites and Bulguksa/Seokguram.

faq.question: Is Andong worth it without a car?
faq.answer: Yes, but harder. Bus 46 runs to Hahoe Village hourly.
